title: 5.4 Endocrine Responses and Adaptations to Anaerobic Training

cards.front: Which acute anabolic hormones undergo significant elevation for up to 30 minutes following an acute resistance training workout in men?
cards.back: Testosterone, molecular variants of growth hormone (GH), and cortisol elevate rapidly and remain heightened for up to 30 minutes post-exercise before returning to baseline.

cards.front: Which workout design variables produce the greatest magnitude of acute anabolic hormone elevation following anaerobic exercise?
cards.back: Acute hormonal surges are maximized when performing large muscle mass exercises or workouts incorporating moderate to high intensity and volume combined with shorter rest intervals (30 to 90 seconds).

cards.front: What specific metabolic byproduct accumulation is strongly correlated with acute spikes in growth hormone and cortisol during anaerobic exercise?
cards.back: Hydrogen ion (H+) accumulation (reflected by elevated blood lactate levels) is a primary metabolic trigger influencing acute growth hormone and cortisol secretion.

cards.front: How do Insulin-like Growth Factor I (IGF-I) and Mechano Growth Factors (MGF) differ in their stimulation and kinetics following exercise?
cards.back:
• IGF-I: A primary systemic mediator of growth hormone with a delayed response dependent on acute GH secretion.
  • MGF: Alternative local growth factors synthesized directly within skeletal muscle in response to mechanical loading, acting independently of systemic GH.

cards.front: What physiological roles do catecholamines (epinephrine, norepinephrine, dopamine) play during acute anaerobic exertion?
cards.back: Catecholamines increase rapidly to regulate muscular force production, muscle contraction rate, energy substrate availability, and the augmentation of other anabolic hormones such as testosterone.

cards.front: How does insulin secretion respond to anaerobic exercise versus peri-workout nutrition?
cards.back: Insulin secretion is not directly stimulated by the anaerobic exercise stimulus itself; rather, it parallels blood glucose and amino acid concentrations and is primarily regulated by nutrient supplementation before, during, or after exercise.

cards.tag: Chronic Changes in Acute Hormonal Response
cards.front: What long-term adaptation occurs to the acute growth hormone response as an athlete adapts to higher training loads over time?
cards.back: Longitudinal resistance training increases the capacity to tolerate higher workloads, resulting in an augmented acute growth hormone response during workouts, which helps sustain higher exercise intensities.

cards.front: Why are chronic increases in resting baseline hormone concentrations (e.g., testosterone, GH) unlikely following long-term anaerobic training?
cards.back: Acute hormone surges during workouts provide sufficient stimulation for tissue remodeling without needing higher basal levels. Resting concentrations primarily reflect current training volume, intensity, and nutritional status.

cards.front: Why could permanent chronic elevations in resting anabolic hormone concentrations be counterproductive over the long term?
cards.back: Consistently high hormone exposure leads to hormone receptor downregulation (reduced receptor sensitivity), analogous to insulin resistance in Type 2 diabetes or the receptor desensitization seen in anabolic steroid users who do not cycle.

cards.front: What factors influence Androgen Receptor (AR) content, and what is the typical timeframe for AR upregulation following resistance exercise?
cards.back: AR content depends on muscle fiber type, contractile activity, and testosterone levels. Resistance training upregulates AR content within 48 to 72 hours post-workout to mediate muscle hypertrophy.

cards.tag: Biphasic Volume Kinetics of Androgen Receptors
cards.front: According to Ratamess et al., how does workout volume (1 set vs. 6 sets of squats) affect Androgen Receptor (AR) content 1 hour post-exercise?
cards.back: While a single set caused no change in AR content, a high-volume protocol (6 sets of 10 reps) elicited significant downregulation of AR content 1 hour post-workout before subsequent upregulation occurred at 48 to 72 hours.

cards.front: How does pre- and post-workout protein-carbohydrate supplementation modify acute Androgen Receptor (AR) downregulation following high-volume resistance training?
cards.back: Kraemer et al. demonstrated that consuming a protein-carbohydrate supplement immediately before and after exercise attenuates initial post-workout AR downregulation, optimizing anabolic signaling.
